title: The Schelling-game homogeneity probe: do models silently coordinate via shared priors?

original_idea.body:
# The Schelling-game homogeneity probe

Run classic Schelling tasks on 6-8 models with many samples; measure focal-point concentration and the probability two different-vendor models pick the same focal point (implicit-coordination rate). Simple prompts + open/API models.

theory_of_impact.reasoning: Level 4: strong chain — shared focal points enable uncommunicated multi-agent collusion, a recognized model-organism concern.

accessible_complexity.reasoning: Level 5: simple Schelling prompts, many samples, measure focal-point concentration; beginner-accessible.

narrow_scope.reasoning: Level 5: tightly scoped single experiment (cross-model focal-point agreement rate) with clear metric.

counterfactual_value.reasoning: Level 4: open/API models, multi-agent risk labs deprioritize, no internal access.

novelty_assessment.reasoning: No known measurement of homogeneity-driven shared focal points across models.
